questions.q: Which sequence describes the k-means loop?
options: Fit a line, measure residuals, add a tree
Merge the two closest rows, repeat until one cluster remains
Assign each row to its nearest centroid, move each centroid to the mean of its rows, repeat until assignments stop changing
Split the data in half, cluster each half, average the results
questions.explain: k-means alternates between assigning rows to the nearest centroid and recomputing each centroid as the mean of its assigned rows.

options: The total squared distance from each row to its assigned centroid, which k-means tries to minimize
The number of rows in the largest cluster
The accuracy against the true labels
The number of iterations run
questions.explain: Inertia is the within-cluster sum of squared distances. Lower is tighter, and it is useful for comparing runs on the same data.

questions.q: In the lesson, one random-start run had inertia 334.76 while the others reached 52.37. What protects you from this in scikit-learn?
options: Scaling the data twice
k-means++ initialization plus n_init, which reruns the algorithm several times and keeps the lowest inertia
Always using k = 1
Removing the random_state argument
questions.explain: k-means++ spreads out the starting centroids and n_init reruns the whole algorithm, keeping the best result.

questions.q: You fit a scaler and k-means on training customers. How should you assign a new customer to a cluster?
options: Fit a new scaler on the single new row, then predict
Skip scaling and call predict directly
Refit k-means including the new customer every time
Transform the new row with the already-fitted scaler, then call predict
questions.explain: New data must go through the same fitted scaler used in training, otherwise its values are on a different scale from the centroids.

questions.q: On two interlocking crescent shapes, k-means with two clusters slices each crescent in half. What does this show?
options: k-means needs more iterations
The scaler was missing
k-means assumes round, similar-sized groups and struggles with non-convex shapes
Inertia was too low
questions.explain: Centroid-based boundaries are straight lines between centers, so non-round shapes are cut incorrectly. DBSCAN or hierarchical methods can suit them better.
